title: Unique Gimmick
text: “Ah, so Sea Otter-Bunny’s the digging position, huh?”
“Dig dig, I say.”
“There might be some gimmick somewhere that only Motoyasu-san can dig through.”
“It’s handy figuring out what everyone can do, but… just what kind of world is this…”
“The mysteries never end.”

Naturally, a Peckle mural showed up. Swimming was its distinguishing feature after all. Having thus figured out each of our respective skills, we pressed further into the labyrinth. And it was there that we spotted some sort of glowing point on the ground.
“Something’s glowing here, I say.”
“Glowing? I don’t see anything.”
“Can’t see it either. Must be one only Motoyasu can spot.”
“Probably so. Motoyasu-kun?”
“Leave it to me, indeed!”
I transformed my spear into a shovel and began digging. Crunch, crunch—what had looked like stone flooring turned to earth and dug right up. Out came some Orichalcum ore!
“Guess that confirms it—Motoyasu’s on excavation duty.”
“Seems like there’ll be spots we can’t pass unless we use our own particular skills.”
Talking things over like that, we pressed on… and came out into a room absolutely filled with needles. Here and there were bits of wall we could grab onto.
“If we go through a place like this, we’re liable to get skewered.”
“Since Motoyasu-kun and Itsuki can fly, safest bet’s probably to cling to those handholds, right?”
While we were discussing that, a sudden gust—whoosh!—erupted from the back of the room, blasting toward the needle-covered sections of the wall.
“Looks like we could brute-force through it, but… it’s pretty blatantly telling me to go. What exactly are they expecting if I fall?”
“Makes you wonder if the needles are instant death or just damage, huh.”
“Please don’t say such unpleasant things. A hero summoned to another world dying because he got stabbed by labyrinth-gimmick needles—don’t even joke about that.”
“Kind of a ‘ti-un ti-un’ vibe, isn’t it?”
“Is that supposed to be some reference gag? Feels like it’d send you right back to the start of the stage or something.”
“Fufu! Well then, allow me to charge in here, I say!”
No need for Itsuki’s heroics—I’d just blast the whole gimmick away with Brionac and charge straight through.
“Brionac, followed by—Flying Mode, I say!”

I launched Brionac straight at the source of the gale, spun my spear, and shifted into Flying Mode to move! With a whoosh the wind died down, but the moment I flew forward, a fresh gust came howling in and sent me slamming into the wall.
“Not gonna happen, I say!”
I tried jamming my spear into a gap between needles to move along, but a needle shot out and jabbed me—prick!
“Owwie, indeed!”
The instant that prick made me jump, I found myself, without realizing it, standing outside the room. The spot where I’d been stuck throbbed with pain.
“I see, I see—so unexpected actions just get you kicked out into the corridor, huh.”
“Literally went ‘ti-un ti-un’ and got booted out of the room.”

Ren said this, using Father’s own phrasing, directed at me as I writhed on the ground clutching my needle-stuck spot in pain. In my memory, the Father-figures from other worlds wryly chuckled about how Motoyasu-kun always gets the tasty roles. I felt like the Father from the very first world, and the one from the world where I reunited with Fleon-chan, were both lamenting, “Why has this guy fallen so far?”—but surely that was just my imagination!
“Motoyasu-san’s useful for experiments like this. Guess it means the same thing would happen to Naofumi-san if there were an underwater gimmick, right?”
“So Motoyasu-kun and the others would drown too, huh—wait, ah!?”
Just then, as Father cautiously peered down at the needle-covered floor, his hand slipped—and he went tumbling right in. Was Father, too, angling for a tasty position here?
“Father!”
I hurriedly reached out, but my hand grasped only air, and Father plunged headfirst straight down onto the needle floor.
“Waaaah!”
And right after Father hit the needle floor—crack, crack!—the needles simply snapped and broke.
“Ow, ow, ow… huh?”
As Father tried to endure the pain and looked around, both Ren and Itsuki’s eyes fell into shadow.
“I suppose because he’s the Shield Hero, the needles are the ones losing this fight.”
“So Naofumi can walk through this kind of instant-death zone without taking a scratch. Is this some kind of gimmick too, or what?”
“Entirely possible, but it’s kind of deflating my whole position here.”
“Hey, someone—! It’s too high, I can’t climb up!”
Having smashed all the needles in the needle-floor zone, Father was now jumping again and again trying to get back to us, but his jump wasn’t quite enough, and he was stuck.
“Why not use Air Strike Shield like stairs to climb up? You’ve got other shields too, don’t you?”
“Ah, right, good point. Air Strike Shield, Second Shield, Trident Shield, then—Change Shield into Rope Shield hook!”
Hop, hop! And just like that, Father made his way back out of the needle-floor zone.
“Well then, Naofumi-san, why don’t you go fetch the item up ahead.”
“I’m not about to pull some tasteless move and steal Itsuki’s spotlight like that.”
“That’s uncalled-for concern!”

In the end, persuaded by Father, Itsuki grabbed onto the wall handholds, made it through the needle zone, and retrieved the item. But it wasn’t Orichalcum ore—instead, he brought back some kind of odd part. The weapon display labeled it as a coelacanth model part.
“Ugh… that’s a suspiciously specific item to find.”
“Since it says ‘model,’ I bet there’s some gimmick somewhere that won’t open unless we collect every single piece.”
“Guess we’ve got no choice but to proceed as expected, then.”
“Well, at least it turned up on the gimmick assigned to Itsuki.”

Father said this with a wry smile. It certainly had been the sort of gimmick that could’ve been substituted with Father instead. After all, once Father walked through and smashed every needle, neither Ren nor I had to bother going through.
“And what exactly are we supposed to do if, instead of some item to turn us back to our original forms, we just keep pulling up mundane tools and ore that don’t matter at all?”
“That’s a complaint you’d want to direct at whoever built this labyrinth, I think.”
“In the end, we’ve got no choice but to keep moving forward… At least having a gamer’s sense of adventure is some small comfort.”
Saying that, Ren walked on with a rather philosophical air. Of course, the rest of us simply carried on as well, pushing forward while fighting off monsters along the way.
“Jumping around as a Peckle earlier was pretty rough. How about the rest of you?”
“Didn’t bother me much, I say.”

“I still feel some unease clinging to walls and jumping and hopping around like that. Since I’m roughly the same build as everyone right now it doesn’t bother me too much, but outside I’m quite a bit shorter, after all.”
“Me, I’m fine, really…”
Ren’s answer trailed off vaguely somehow.
“Could it be that even in Inult form you can adapt to the movement fairly well because of your VR experience back in Japan?”
Ren swiftly turned his face away. Whenever the topic of his VR gaming experience came up, Ren seemed to get evasive about it much the same way Itsuki got evasive talking about his family.
“I see, an avatar within the internet, is it? In my world too, there’s a thing where you set your icon to a favorite character, but depending on the item, some of them can get pretty fancy.”
“……Right. Aside from playing VR games, when diving into the net you set up an avatar, and you can change it around however you feel like at the time.”
“Sounds kind of dreamy, doesn’t it. I’ve been curious about this for a while now—what kind of history led to the development of VR games in your world, Ren, before they came out into the world?”
“That does make me curious too.”
“As for the Dimension Wave that Itsuki was involved in, Father already got the details out of Itsuki back in the very first world, so I already know about that one, I say.”
“Well, if we’re looping, it’s not strange that some version of me elsewhere already explained it.”
“I’m curious about Itsuki’s case too, though—what was it again?”
Father asked Ren and Itsuki with eyes brimming full of curiosity. And here, too, was a moment for me to make my own case, indeed.
